content.value_statement: Analytics teams need repeatable dbt patterns for models, tests, and documentation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical transformation design.
actual_capabilities: Defines dbt layer patterns for staging, intermediate, and mart models.
Shows source definitions with freshness checks and column tests.
Explains staging and mart model examples for Stripe and Shopify data.
Covers dbt tests, documentation files, and common dbt-utils checks.
Provides macro examples for reusable SQL and development data limits.
Compares incremental strategies such as merge, delete and insert, and partition overwrite.
limitations: Does not connect to a warehouse or run dbt commands by itself.
Requires users to adapt examples to their schema and adapter.
Does not replace data governance, access control, or production review.
Examples focus on common analytics models, not every dbt package.

use_cases.title: Plan a new dbt project
use_cases.description: Map sources, staging models, intermediate models, and marts before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize modeling conventions
use_cases.description: Create shared naming, layering, test, and documentation patterns for a growing data team.

use_cases.title: Improve dbt build quality
use_cases.description: Add tests, freshness checks, documentation, and incremental strategies to existing models.

prompt_templates.title: Design model layers
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new warehouse-backed dbt project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbt transformation patterns to propose staging, intermediate, and mart layers for my sources: [list sources]. Include naming conventions and ownership notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add tests and documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate improvement for existing dbt models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these dbt model goals: [describe models]. Recommend column tests, relationship tests, freshness checks, and documentation coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Choose incremental strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance planning for large tables.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a dbt incremental strategy for [table name]. Consider data volume, late-arriving records, unique keys, partitions, and full-refresh risks.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor transformation logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup of duplicated analytics logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this dbt transformation design: [paste summary]. Suggest staging cleanup, intermediate models, macros, tests, and migration steps.

output_examples.input: A team has raw Stripe and Shopify data and wants a core customer mart.
output: A layer plan with Stripe and Shopify staging models.
An intermediate payment summary grouped by customer.
A customer dimension with uniqueness, relationship, and freshness checks.

output_examples.input: A large event table needs faster daily dbt builds.
output: A recommendation to evaluate an incremental materialization.
Guidance on unique keys, partitions, and late-arriving records.
A reminder to test full-refresh behavior before production use.

output_examples.input: Existing marts repeat currency conversion and development filters.
output: A macro extraction plan for shared conversion logic.
A development data limit pattern for faster local runs.
A testing checklist to prevent behavior changes during refactoring.

best_practices: Start with clear source definitions, freshness rules, and tested primary keys.
Keep staging models simple and move business logic into intermediate models.
Document models and columns while adding tests for important assumptions.
anti_patterns: Building marts directly from raw sources without a staging layer.
Hardcoding dates, schemas, or environment-specific values in reusable models.
Copying transformation logic across models instead of using intermediate models or macros.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design dbt models, tests, documentation, macros, and incremental patterns for analytics engineering projects.

faq.question: Can it run dbt commands for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples, but users decide what to run in their environment.

faq.question: Which dbt layers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers source definitions, staging models, intermediate models, marts, tests, documentation, and macros.

faq.question: Does it support incremental models?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common incremental strategies and when to consider each option.

faq.question: Is this useful for non-dbt SQL projects?
faq.answer: Only partly. The guidance assumes dbt project structure, references, tests, and materializations.

faq.question: Can teams adapt the examples?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams should replace sample sources, keys, and tests with their warehouse schema and business rules.
